title: fix(tty): fall back to default dimensions when terminal size is 0x0
body:
### Problem

When running Bubble Tea v2 applications on serial consoles, headless setups, or terminals where window dimensions are not yet configured or reported as 0x0 (e.g. stty rows 0 cols 0), term.GetSize returns (0, 0, nil). Bubble Tea sets p.width = 0 and p.height = 0 and passes these dimensions to the renderer and model. Because the viewport height and width are 0, rendered output lines are clipped, resulting in a completely blank screen.

### Root Cause

In Program.Run and Program.checkResize:
- term.GetSize(p.ttyOutput.Fd()) can return (0, 0, nil) or non-positive values without returning an error.
- Previously, these dimensions were assigned directly to p.width and p.height without verifying they are positive.
- When s.height is 0 in cursedRenderer, line buffering clips lines, producing no visible content.

### Solution

1. Added fallbackDimensions(width, height int) (int, int) helper on *Program with standard terminal defaults (defaultWidth = 80, defaultHeight = 24).
2. If width <= 0, fall back to COLUMNS (checking program environment first, then os.Getenv) if positive, otherwise fall back to 80.
3. If height <= 0, fall back to LINES (checking program environment first, then os.Getenv) if positive, otherwise fall back to 24.
4. Applied fallback in both Program.Run and Program.checkResize.
5. Added unit tests in tty_test.go covering fallback to 80x24, fallback to COLUMNS/LINES, handling invalid or zero env values, and initial window size message dispatch.

Fixes #1828

issues.title: v2: blank screen when tty size is 0x0 (e.g. in a serial console)

evidence.body: This fallback also runs when the output isn't a terminal at all, such as output to a buffer, a pipe, or a Wish/SSH session. Apps that used to receive a 0x0 size there will now get a made-up 80x24. Moving this line inside the `if p.ttyOutput != nil` block above would limit the fix to the actual bug
